title: Injectivity from the closed fibre over a valuation ring
statement: Let $A$ be a valuation ring, meaning an integral domain for which each nonzero element $a$ of its fraction field satisfies $a\in A$ or $a^{-1}\in A$. Let $A\to B$ be a local homomorphism of commutative local rings (the inverse image of the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_B$ is $\mathfrak m_A$), essentially of finite type [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra]. Let $N,M$ be finite $B$-modules [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and $u:N\to M$ a $B$-linear map. Suppose $M$, with scalars restricted to $A$, is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and that the induced map $N/\mathfrak m_AN\to M/\mathfrak m_AM$ is injective, where $\mathfrak m_AN$ and $\mathfrak m_AM$ denote the submodules generated by products of elements of $\mathfrak m_A$ with module elements. Then $u$ is injective and the $A$-module $M/u(N)$ is flat.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-local-essentially-finite-type-polynomial-cover] to the given local essentially finite type map. Obtain $P=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, a prime $\mathfrak q$, and a surjective local $A$-algebra map $\pi:S=P_{\mathfrak q}\twoheadrightarrow B$, with $A\to S$ local and essentially of finite presentation.

Restrict the actions on $N,M$ along $\pi$. If $y=\sum_j b_j y_j$ in either module for a finite $B$-generating family $(y_j)$, choose $s_j\in S$ with $\pi(s_j)=b_j$. Then $y=\sum_j s_j y_j$, proving finiteness over $S$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. The map $u$ is $S$-linear. The underlying $A$-modules, the submodules $\mathfrak m_A N,\mathfrak m_A M$, the fibre map and the quotient $M/u(N)$ are unchanged. Thus the flat-target and injective-fibre hypotheses hold over $A\to S$.

proof.text: A finite algebra presentation exhibits the algebra as generated by the finitely many variable images [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Thus the localization $S$ from Step 1 is essentially of finite type [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra]. Apply [lem-trf-valuation-flat-finite-module-presentation] to $A\to S$ and $M$: locality holds by Step 1, and Step 2 supplies finiteness over $S$ and flatness over the valuation base $A$. Hence $M$ is finitely presented over $S$. Apply [lem-trf-valuation-fibre-injective-source-presentation] to the same map and $u:N\to M$. Its local essentially-finitely-presented hypothesis is Step 1; its two finite modules, flat target and injective closed fibre are Step 2. Hence $N$ is finitely presented over $S$ as well.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-valuation-general-mod-injective] with $R=A$ and algebra $S$; its source $M$ is our $N$, its target $N$ is our $M$, and its map is $u$. Step 1 gives the local essentially finitely presented algebra. Step 3 gives finite presentation of both modules. Step 2 identifies the base-maximal-ideal quotients, so the required fibre map is exactly the assumed injective map; the target remains $A$-flat. The criterion gives injectivity of $u$ and $A$-flatness of $M/u(N)$, on the unchanged underlying $A$-modules.
